answer: A practical anti-sybil defence is to give each agent identity a pigment-like fingerprint earned through sustained, verifiable work — a reputation that cannot be painted on overnight. Think of trust as a knoll built layer by layer, from audited tasks and real transactions; new accounts start with tight limits and earn wider access only as their history grows. A sudden whisper of thousands of fresh accounts then costs real time and effort to make credible, while honest agents keep the standing they built. Sybils become expensive to spawn at scale, and misbehaviour forfeits the reputation.
